figures.caption: Fig. 2. Comparison of a He I UPS spectrum plotted with respect to the Fermi level (left ordinate) and with respect to the vacuum level (right ordinate). “Binding Energy” is used to designate the energy referenced to the Fermi level, and “Ionization Energy” is used to designate the energy referenced to the vacuum level. Notice that when plotted with respect to the latter, the SECO corresponds to the photon energy.

figures.caption: Fig. 3. a) Approximately normalized UPS spectra of sputtered Ag foil obtained with a He discharge lamp operating at normal and low pressures, plotted with respect to photoelectron kinetic energy; ten scans were averaged for each spectrum. b) Approximately normalized He I and He II UPS of the Ag 4d region, plotted with respect to the Fermi level. The “He I Spectrum” scan is extracted from the data in a), while the “He II Spectrum” scan is a different data set in which 27 scans were averaged. The horizontal arrows point to the ordinate scale used for a particular spectrum. These data were acquired on a VG Scientific MKII ESCALAB with a concentric hemispherical energy analyzer operating in FAT mode, with a pass energy of 2 eV and a sample bias of −6.19 V. figures.caption: Fig. 8. He I UPS data for clean W(110), chemisorbed pyridine on W(110), and physisorbed pyridine on W(110), with all surfaces at 90 K. The entire spectra are shown in a), and the SECO cutoffs and calculated work functions are shown in b). Chemisorbed pyridine surface was prepared by heating multilayer pyridine to 190 K for 30 s to desorb physisorbed pyridine and leave a monolayer of chemisorbed pyridine. These data were acquired using a Physical Electronics double pass CMA spectrometer (retard ratio of 2), with the sample biased at −6.40 V relative to ground. The binding energy scale is referenced to the Fermi level. 9
